1.1: It came to pass in the thirtieth yere in the fourth moneth, and in the fift day of the moneth (as I was among the captives by the river Chebar) that the heavens were opened and I saw visions of GOD.
1.2: In the fift day of the moneth (which was the fift yere of King Ioiachins captiuitie)
1.3: The word of the Lord came unto Ezekiel the Priest, the sonne of Buzi, in the land of the Caldeans, by the river Chebar, where the hand of the Lord was upon him.
1.4: And I looked, and behold, a whirlewinde came out of the North, a great cloud and a fire wrapped about it, and a brightness was about it, and in the middes thereof, to wit, in the middes of the fire came out as the likeness of amber.
1.5: Also out of the middes therof came the likeness of four beastes, and this was their form: they had the appearance of a man.
1.6: And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.
1.7: And their feet were streight feet, and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calves foot, and they sparkled like the appearance of bright brass.
1.8: And the handes of a man came out from under their wings in the four parts of them, and they four had their faces, and their wings.
1.9: They where ioyned by their wings one to another, and when they went forth, they returned not, but every one went streight forward.
1.10: And the similitude of their faces was as the face of a man: and they four had the face of a lyon on the right side, and they four had the face of a bullock on the left side: they four also had the face of an eagle.
1.11: Thus were their faces: but their wings were spred out above: two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies.
1.12: And every one went streight forward: they went whither their spirit led them, and they returned not when they went forth.
1.13: The similitude also of the beasts, and their appearance was like burning coles of fire, and like the appearance of lampes: for the fire ran among the beastes, and the fire gave a glister, and out of the fire there went lightning.
1.14: And the beastes ranne, and returned like unto lightning.
1.15: Now as I beheld the beastes, behold, a wheel appeared upon the earth by the beastes, having four faces.
1.16: The facion of the wheeles and their work was like unto a chrysolite: and they four had one form, and their facion, and their work was as one wheel in another wheel.
1.17: Whe they went, they went upon their four sides, and they returned not when they went.
1.18: They had also rings, and height, and were fearefull to behold, and their rings were full of eyes, round about them four.
1.19: And when the beastes went, the wheeles went with them: and when the beasts were lift up from the earth, the wheeles were lift up.
1.20: Whither the spirit led them, they went, and thither did the spirit of the wheeles lead them, and the wheeles were lifted up besides them: for the spirit of the beastes was in the wheeles.
1.21: When the beastes went, they went, and when they stood, they stood, and when they were lifted up from the earth, the wheeles were lifted up besides them: for the spirit of the beastes was in the wheeles.
1.22: And the similitude of the firmament upon the heads of the beasts was wonderful, like unto chrystall, spred over their heads above.
1.23: And under the firmament were their wings streight, the one toward the other: every one had two, which covered the, and every one had two, which covered their bodies.
1.24: And when they went foorth, I heard the noyse of their wings, like the noyse of great waters, and as the voyce of the Almightie, even the voyce of speach, as the noyse of an host: and when they stood, they let down their wings.
1.25: And there was a voyce from the firmament, that was over their heads, when they stood, and had let down their wings.
1.26: And above the firmament that was over their heads, was the facion of a throne like unto a saphir stone, and upon the similitude of the throne was by appearance, as the similitude of a man above upon it.
1.27: And I saw as the appearance of amber, and as the similitude of fire round about within it to look to, even from his loynes vpwarde: and to look to, even from his loynes downewarde, I saw as a likeness of fire, and brightness round about it.
1.28: As the likeness of the bow, that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the light round about.
1.29: This was the appearance of the similitude of the glorie of the Lord: and when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voyce of one that spake.

2.1: And he said unto me, Sonne of man, stand up upon thy feet, and I wil speak unto thee.
2.2: And the Spirit entred into me, when he had spoken unto me, and set me upon my feet, so that I heard him that spake unto me.
2.3: And he said unto me, Sonne of man, I send thee to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that hath rebelled against me: for they and their fathers have rebelled against me, even unto this very day.
2.4: For they are impudent children, and stiff hearted: I do send thee unto them, and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God.
2.5: But surely they will not hear, neither in deed will they cease: for they are a rebellious house: yet shall they know that there hath been a Prophet among them.
2.6: And thou sonne of man, fear them not, neither be afraid of their wordes, although rebels, and thornes be with thee, and thou remainest with scorpions: fear not their wordes, nor be afrayde at their lookes, for they are a rebellious house.
2.7: Therefore thou shalt speak my words unto them: but surely they will not hear, neither will they in deed cease: for they are rebellious.
2.8: But thou sonne of man, hear what I say unto thee: be not thou rebellious, like this rebellious house: open thy mouth, and eat that I give thee.
2.9: And when I looked up, behold, an hand was sent unto me, and loe, a roule of a book was therein.
2.10: And he spred it before me, and it was written within and without, and there was written therein, Lamentations, and mourning, and woe.

3.1: Moreover he said unto me, Sonne of man, eat that thou findest: eat this roule, and goe, and speak unto the house of Israel.
3.2: So I opened my mouth, and he gave mee this roule to eat.
3.3: And he said unto me, Sonne of man, cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roule that I give thee. Then did I eat it, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honie.
3.4: And he said unto me, Sonne of man, goe, and enter into the house of Israel, and declare them my wordes.
3.5: For thou art not sent to a people of an vnknowen tongue, or of an hard language, but to the house of Israel,
3.6: Not to many people of an vnknowen tongue, or of an hard language, whose wordes thou canst not understand: yet if I should send thee to them, they would obey thee.
3.7: But the house of Israel will not obey thee: for they will not obey me: yea, all the house of Israel are impudent and stiff hearted.
3.8: Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead hard against their foreheads.
3.9: I have made thy forehead as the adamant, and harder then the flint: fear them not therefore, neither be afraid at their lookes: for they are a rebellious house.
3.10: He said moreover unto me, Sonne of man, receive in thine heart al my words that I speak unto thee, and hear them with thine eares,
3.11: And goe and enter to them that are led away captives unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God: but surely they will not hear, neither will they in deed cease.
3.12: Then the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me a noise of a great rushing, saying, Blessed be ye glorie of the Lord out of his place.
3.13: I heard also the noyse of the wings of the beasts, that touched one another, and the ratling of the wheeles that were by them, even a noyse of a great rushing.
3.14: So the spirit lift me up, and took me away and I went in bitterness, and indignation of my spirit, but the hand of the Lord was strong upon me.
3.15: Then I came to them that were led away captives to Tel-abib, that dwelt by the river Chebar, and I sat where they sat, and remained there astonished among them seven dayes.
3.16: And at the end of seven dayes, the word of the Lord came again unto me, saying,
3.17: Sonne of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.
3.18: When I shall say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die, and thou givest not him warning, nor speakest to admonish the wicked of his wicked way, that he may live, the same wicked man shall die in his iniquitie: but his blood will I require at thine hand.
3.19: Yet if thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquitie, but thou hast delivered thy soul.
3.20: Likewise if a righteous man turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquitie, I will lay a stumbling blocke before him, and he shall die, because thou hast not given him warning: he shall die in his sinne, and his righteous deedes, which he hath done, shall not be remembred: but his blood will I require at thine hand.
3.21: Nevertheless, if thou admonish that righteous man, that the righteous sinne not, and that he doeth not sinne, he shall live because he is admonished: also thou hast delivered thy soul.
3.22: And the hand of the Lord was there upon me, and he said unto me, Arise, and goe into the field, and I will there talk with thee.
3.23: So when I had risen up, and gone foorth into the field, behold, the glorie of the Lord stood there, as the glorie which I saw by the river Chebar, and I fell down upon my face.
3.24: Then the Spirit entred into me, which set me up upon my feet, and spake unto me, and said to me, Come, and shut thy self within thine house.
3.25: But thou, O sonne of man, behold, they shall put bandes upon thee, and shall bind thee with them, and thou shalt not goe out among them.
3.26: And I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dume, and shalt not be to them as a man that rebuketh: for they are a rebellious house.
3.27: But when I shall have spoken unto thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God, He that heareth, let him hear, and he that leaveth off, let him leave: for they are a rebellious house.

4.1: Thou also sonne of man, take thee a brick, and lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the citie, even Jerusalem,
4.2: And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it: set the camp also against it, and lay engins of war against it round about.
4.3: Moreover, take an yron pan, and set it for a wall of yron between thee and the citie, and direct thy face toward it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it: this shall be a sign unto the house of Israel.
4.4: Sleep thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquitie of the house of Israel upon it: according to the nomber of the dayes, that thou shalt sleep upon it, thou shalt bear their iniquity.
4.5: For I have layed upon thee the yeeres of their iniquitie, according to the nomber of the dayes, even three hundreth and ninetie dayes: so shalt thou bear the iniquitie of the house of Israel.
4.6: And when thou hast accomplished them, sleep again upon thy right side, and thou shalt bear the iniquitie of the house of Judah fourtie dayes: I have appointed thee a day for a yeere, even a day for a yeere.
4.7: Therefore thou shalt direct thy face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and thine arm shalbe vncouered, and thou shalt prophesie against it.
4.8: And behold, I will lay bands upon thee, and thou shalt not turn thee from one side to another, till thou hast ended the dayes of thy siege.
4.9: Thou shalt take also unto thee wheat, and barley, and beanes, and lentiles, and millet, and fitches, and put them in one vessell, and make thee bread thereof according to the nomber of the dayes, that thou shalt sleep upon thy side: even three hundreth and ninetie dayes shalt thou eat thereof.
4.10: And the meat, whereof thou shalt eat, shalbe by weight, even twenty shekels a day: and from time to time shalt thou eat thereof.
4.11: Thou shalt drink also water by measure, even the sixt part of an Hin: from time to time shalt thou drink.
4.12: And thou shalt eat it as barley cakes, and thou shalt bake it in the dongue that cometh out of man, in their sight.
4.13: And the Lord said, So shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will cast them.
4.14: Then said I, Ah, Lord God, behold, my soul hath not been polluted: for from my youth up, even unto this hour, I have not eaten of a thing dead, or torn in pieces, neither came there any vncleane flesh in my mouth.
4.15: Then he said unto me, Loe, I have given thee bullockes dongue for mans dongue, and thou shalt prepare thy bread therewith.
4.16: Moreover, he said unto me, Sonne of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem, and they shall eat bread by weight, and with care, and they shall drink water by measure, and with astonishment.
4.17: Because that bread and water shall fail, they shalbe astonied one with another, and shall consume away for their iniquitie.

5.1: And thou sonne of man, take thee a sharp knife, or take thee a barbours rasor and cause it to pass upon thine head, and upon thy beard: then take thee balances to weigh, and deuide the hear.
5.2: Thou shalt burn with fire the third part in the middes of the citie, when the dayes of the siege are fulfilled, and thou shalt take the other third part, and smite about it with a knife, and the last third part thou shalt scatter in the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
5.3: Thou shalt also take thereof a few in nomber, and bind them in thy lappe.
5.4: Then take of them again and cast them into the middes of the fire, and burn them in the fire: for thereof shall a fire come foorth into all the house of Israel.
5.5: Thus saith the Lord God, This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the middes of the nations and countreyes, that are round about her.
5.6: And she hath changed my iudgements into wickednes more then the nations, and my statutes more then the countreis, that are round about her: for they have refused my iudgemets and my statutes, and they have not walked in them.
5.7: Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Because your multitude is greater then the nations that are round about you, and ye have not walked in my statutes, neither have ye kept my iudgements: no, ye have not done according to the iudgements of the nations, that are round about you,
5.8: Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I, even I come against thee, and will execute iudgement in the middes of thee, even in the sight of the nations.
5.9: And I will doe in thee, that I never did before, neither will do any more the like, because of all thine abominations.
5.10: For in the middes of thee, the fathers shall eat their sonnes, and the sonnes shall eat their fathers, and I will execute iudgement in thee, and the whole remnant of thee will I scatter into all the windes.
5.11: Wherefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, Surely because thou hast defiled my Sanctuarie with all thy filthiness, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also destroy thee, neither shall mine eye spare thee, neither will I have any pitie.
5.12: The third part of thee shall die with the pestilence, and with famine shall they bee consumed in the middes of thee: and another third part shall fall by the sword round about thee: and I will scatter the last third part into all windes, and I will draw out a sword after them.
5.13: Thus shall mine anger bee accomplished, and I will cause my wrath to cease in them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know, that I the Lord have spoke it in my zeal, when I have accomplished my wrath in them.
5.14: Moreover, I will make thee waste, and abhorred among the nations, that are round about thee, and in the sight of all that pass by.
5.15: So thou shalt bee a reproche and shame, a chastisement and an astonishment unto the nations, that are round about thee, when I shall execute iudgements in thee, in anger and in wrath, and in sharp rebukes: I the Lord have spoken it.
5.16: When I shall send upon them the evil arrowes of famine, which shalbe for their destruction, and which I will send to destroy you: and I will encrease the famine upon you, and wil break your staff of bread.
5.17: So will I send upon you famine, and evil beastes, and they shall spoyle thee, and pestilence and blood shall pass through thee, and I will bring the sword upon thee: I the Lord have spoken it.

6.1: Again the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
6.2: Sonne of man, Set thy face towardes the mountaines of Israel, and prophecie against them,
6.3: And say, Ye mountaines of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: thus sayth the Lord God to the mountaines and to the hilles, to the rivers and to the valleis, Behold, I, even I will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your hie places:
6.4: And your altars shalbe desolate, and your images of the sunne shalbe broken: and I will cast down your slain men before your idoles.
6.5: And I will lay the dead carkeises of the children of Israel before their idoles, and I will scatter your bones round about your altars.
6.6: In all your dwelling places the cities shalbe desolate, and the hie places shalbe laid waste, so that your altars shalbe made waste and desolate, and your idoles shalbe broken, and cease, and your images of the sunne shalbe cut in pieces, and your workes shalbe abolished.
6.7: And the slain shall fall in the middes of you, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
6.8: Yet will I leave a remnant, that you may have some that shall escape the sword among the nations, when you shalbe scattred through the countreyes.
6.9: And they that escape of you, shall remember me among the nations, where they shalbe in captiuitie, because I am grieved for their whorish hearts, which have departed from mee, and for their eyes, which have gone a whoring after their idoles, and they shalbe displeased in them selves for the evils, which they have committed in all their abominations.
6.10: And they shall know that I am the Lord, and that I have not said in vain, that I would doe this evil unto them.
6.11: Thus saith the Lord God, Smite with thine hand, and stretch forth with thy foot, and say, Alas, for all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel: for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.
6.12: He that is far off, shall dye of the pestilence, and he that is neere, shall fall by the sword, and hee that remaineth and is besieged, shall dye by the famine: thus will I accomplish my wrath upon them.
6.13: Then ye shall know, that I am ye Lord, when their slain men shalbe among their idoles round about their altars, upon euerie hie hill in al the toppes of the mountaines, and under every green tree, and under euerie thick oke, which is the place where they did offer sweet sauour to all their idoles.
6.14: So will I stretch mine hand upon them, and make the land waste, and desolate from the wildernes unto Diblath in all their habitations, and they shall know, that I am the Lord.

7.1: Moreover the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
7.2: Also thou sonne of man, thus saith the Lord God, An end is come unto the land of Israel: the end is come upon the four corners of the land.
7.3: Now is the end come upon thee, and I wil send my wrath upon thee, and will judge thee according to thy wayes, and will lay upon thee all thine abominations.
7.4: Neither shall mine eye spare thee, neither will I have pitie: but I will lay thy waies upon thee: and thine abomination shall bee in the middes of thee, and yee shall know that I am the Lord.
7.5: Thus saith the Lord God, Behold, one evil, even one evil is come.
7.6: An end is come, the end is come, it watched for thee: behold, it is come.
7.7: The morning is come unto thee, that dwellest in the land: the time is come, the day of trouble is neere, and not the sounding again of the mountaines.
7.8: Now I will shortly powre out my wrath upon thee, and fulfil mine anger upon thee: I will judge thee according to thy wayes, and will lay upon thee all thine abominations.
7.9: Neither shall mine eie spare thee, neither will I have pitie, but I will lay upon thee according to thy wayes, and thine abominations shalbe in the middes of thee, and ye shall know that I am the Lord that smiteth.
7.10: Behold, the day, behold, it is come: the morning is gone forth, the rod florisheth: pride hath budded.
7.11: Crueltie is risen up into a rod of wickednes: none of them shall remain, nor of their riches, nor of any of theirs, neither shall there bee lamentation for them.
7.12: The time is come, the day draweth neere: let not the byer reioyce, nor let him that selleth, mourn: for the wrath is upon al the multitude thereof.
7.13: For hee that selleth, shall not return to that which is sold, although they were yet alive: for the vision was unto al the multitude thereof, and they returned not, neither doeth any encourage himself in the punishment of his life.
7.14: They have blowen the trumpet, and prepared all, but none goeth to the battel: for my wrath is upon all the multitude thereof.
7.15: The sword is without, and the pestilence, and the famine within: he that is in the field, shall dye with the sword, and he that is in the citie, famine and pestilence shall deuoure him.
7.16: But they that flee away from them, shall escape, and shalbe in the mountaines, like the doves of the valleis: all they shall mourn, every one for his iniquitie.
7.17: All handes shalbe weak, and all knees shall fall away as water.
7.18: They shall also gird them selves with sackecloth, and fear shall cover them, and shame shalbe upon all faces, and baldnes upon their heads.
7.19: They shall cast their silver in the streetes, and their gold shalbe cast far off: their silver and their gold can not deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord: they shall not satisfie their soules, neither fill their bowels: for this ruin is for their iniquitie.
7.20: He had also set the beautie of his ornament in maiestie: but they made images of their abominations, and of their idoles therein: therefore have I set it far from them.
7.21: And I will give it into the handes of the strangers to be spoyled, and to the wicked of the earth to be robbed, and they shall pollute it.
7.22: My face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret place: for the destroyers shall enter into it, and defile it.
7.23: Make a chain: for the land is full of the iudgement of blood, and the citie is full of crueltie.
7.24: Wherefore I will bring the most wicked of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pomp of the mightie to cease, and their holie places shalbe defiled.
7.25: When destruction cometh, they shall seek peace, and shall not have it.
7.26: Calamitie shall come upon calamitie, and rumour shall bee upon rumour: then shall they seek a vision of the Prophet: but the Law shall perish from the Priest, and counsel from the Ancient.
7.27: The King shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the handes of the people in the land shall be troubled: I wil doe unto them according to their waies, and according to their iudgements will I judge them, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

8.1: And in the sixt yere, in the sixt moneth, and in the fift day of the moneth, as I sat in mine house, and the Elders of Judah sat before me, the hand of the Lord God fell there upon me.
8.2: Then I beheld, and lo, there was a likeness, as the appearance of fire, to look to, from his loynes downeward, and from his loynes upward, as the appearance of brightnes, and like unto amber.
8.3: And he stretched out the likenes of an had, and took me by an hearie lock of mine head, and the Spirit lift me up between the earth, and the heaven, and brought mee by a Divine vision to Jerusalem, into the entry of ye inner gate that lieth toward the North, where remained the idol of indignation, which provoked indignation.
8.4: And behold, the glorie of the God of Israel was there according to the vision, that I saw in the field.
8.5: Then said he unto mee, Sonne of man, lift up thine eyes now toward the North. So I lift up mine eyes toward the North, and behold, Northward, at the gate of the altar, this idol of indignation was in the entrie.
8.6: He said furthermore unto me, Sonne of man, seest thou not what they doe? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here to cause me to depart from my Sanctuarie? but yet turn thee and thou shalt see greater abominations.
8.7: And he caused me to enter at the gate of the court: and when I looked, behold, an hole was in the wall.
8.8: Then said he unto me, Sonne of man, digge now in the wall. And when I had digged in the wall, behold, there was a door.
8.9: And he said unto mee, Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they doe here.
8.10: So I went in, and saw, and behold, there was every similitude of creeping thinges and abominable beasts and all the idoles of the house of Israel painted upon the wall round about.
8.11: And there stood before them seuentie men of the Ancients of the house of Israel, and in the middes of them stood Jaazaniah, ye sonne of Shaphan, with euerie man his censour in his hand, and the vapour of the incense went up like a cloud.
8.12: Then said hee unto mee, Sonne of man, hast thou seen what the Ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every one in the chamber of his imagerie? for they say, The Lord seeth us not, the Lord hath forsaken the earth.
8.13: Again he said also unto me, Turn thee again, and thou shalt see greater abominations that they doe.
8.14: And he caused me to enter into the entrie of the gate of the Lords house, which was toward the North: and behold there sat women mourning for Tammuz.
8.15: Then said hee unto me, Hast thou seen this, O sonne of man? Turn thee again, and thou shalt see greater abominations then these.
8.16: And he caused me to enter into the inner court of the Lordes house, and behold, at the door of the Temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar were about five and twentie men with their backs toward the Temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the East, and they worshipped the sunne, toward the East.
8.17: The he said unto me, Hast thou seen this, O sonne of man? Is it a small thing to the house of Judah to commit these abominations which they do here? for they have filled the land with crueltie, and have returned to provoke mee: and loe, they have cast out stink before their noses.
8.18: Therefore will I also execute my wrath: mine eye shall not spare them, neither will I have pitie, and though they crie in mine eares with a loud voyce, yet will I not hear them.

9.1: He cryed also with a loud voyce in mine eares, saying, The visitations of the citie draw neere, and every man hath a weapon in his hand to destroy it.
9.2: And behold, six men came by the way of the hie gate, which lieth toward the North, and every man a weapon in his hand to destroy it: and one man among them was clothed with linen, with a writers ynkhorne by his side, and they went in and stood beside the brasen altar.
9.3: And the glorie of the God of Israel was gone up from ye Cherub, whereupon he was and stood on the door of the house, and he called to the man clothed with linen, which had the writers ynkhorne by his side.
9.4: And the Lord said unto him, Goe through the middes of the citie, even through the middes of Jerusalem and set a mark upon the foreheads of them that mourn, and cry for all the abominations that be done in the middes thereof.
9.5: And to the other he said, that I might hear, Goe ye after him through the citie, and smite: let your eye spare none, neither have pitie.
9.6: Destroy utterly the old, and the yong, and the maides, and the children, and the women, but touch no man, upon whom is the mark, and begin at my Sanctuarie. Then they began at the Ancient men, which were before the house.
9.7: And he sayde unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courtes with the slain, then goe foorth: and they went out, and slew them in the citie.
9.8: Now when they had slain them, and I had escaped, I fell down upon my face, and cryed, saying, Ah Lord God, wilt thou destroy all the residue of Israel, in powring out thy wrath upon Jerusalem?
9.9: Then said he unto me, The iniquitie of the house of Israel, and Judah is exceeding great, so that the land is full of blood, and the citie full of corrupt iudgement: for they say, The Lord hath forsaken the earth, and the Lord seeth us not.
9.10: As touching me also, mine eye shall not spare them, neither will I have pitie, but will recompence their wayes upon their heades.
9.11: And behold, the man clothed with linen which had the ynkhorne by his side, made report, and said, Lord, I have done as thou hast commanded me.

10.1: And as I looked, behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the Cherubims there appeared upon them like unto the similitude of a throne, as it were a saphir stone.
10.2: And he spake unto the man clothed with linen, and said, Go in between the wheeles, even under the Cherub, and fill thine hands with coales of fire from between the Cherubims, and scatter the over the citie. And he went in in my sight.
10.3: Now the Cherubims stood upon the right side of the house, when the man went in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
10.4: Then the glorie of the Lord went up from the Cherub, and stood over the door of the house, and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the Lordes glorie.
10.5: And the sound of the Cherubims wings was heard into the utter court, as the voyce of the Almightie God, when he speaketh.
10.6: And when he had commanded the man clothed with linen, saying, Take fire from between the wheeles, and from between ye Cherubims, then he went in and stood beside ye wheel.
10.7: And one Cherub stretched forth his hand from between the Cherubims unto the fire, that was between the Cherubims, and took thereof, and put it into the hands of him that was clothed with linen: who took it and went out.
10.8: And there appeared in the Cherubims, the likeness of a mans hand under their wings.
10.9: And when I looked up, behold, four wheeles were beside the Cherubims, one wheel by one Cherub, and another wheel by another Cherub, and the appearance of the wheeles was as the colour of a Chrysolite stone.
10.10: And their appearance (for they were all four of one facion) was as if one wheel had been in another wheel.
10.11: When they went foorth, they went upon their four sides, and they returned not as they went: but to the place whither the first went, they went after it, and they turned not as they went.
10.12: And their whole bodie, and their rings, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheeles were full of eyes round about, even in the same four wheeles.
10.13: And the Cherub cryed to these wheeles in mine hearing, saying, O wheel.
10.14: And every beast had four faces: the first face was the face of a Cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lyon, and the fourth the face of an Egle.
10.15: And the Cherubims were lifted up: this is the beast that I saw at the river Chebar.
10.16: And when ye Cherubims went, the wheeles went by them: and when the Cherubims lift up their wings to mount up from the earth, the same wheeles also turned not from beside them.
10.17: When the Cherubims stood, they stood: and when they were lifted up, they lifted the selves up also: for the spirit of the beast was in them.
10.18: Then the glorie of the Lord departed from above the door of the house, and stood upon the Cherubims.
10.19: And the Cherubims lift up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight: when they went out, the wheeles also were besides them: and every one stood at the entrie of the gate of the Lordes House at the East side, and the glorie of the God of Israel was upon them on hie.
10.20: This is the beast that I saw under the God of Israel by the river Chebar, and I knew that they were the Cherubims.
10.21: Every one had four faces, and every one four wings, and the likeness of mans hands was under their wings.
10.22: And the likeness of their faces was the self same faces, which I saw by the river Chebar, and the appearance of the Cherubims was ye self same, and they went every one straight forward.

11.1: Moreover, the Spirit lift me up, and brought me unto the East gate of the Lordes house, which lyeth Eastward, and behold, at the entrie of the gate were five and twentie men: among whom I saw Jaazaniah the sonne of Azur, and Pelatiah the sonne of Benaiah, the princes of the people.
11.2: Then said he unto me, Sonne of man, these are the men that imagine mischief, and devise wicked counsel in this citie.
11.3: For they say, It is not neere, let us build houses: this citie is the caldron, and wee be the flesh.
11.4: Therefore prophesie against them, sonne of man, prophesie.
11.5: And the Spirit of the Lord fell upon me, and said unto me, Speak, Thus saith the Lord, O ye house of Israel, this have ye said, and I know that which riseth up of your mindes.
11.6: Many have ye murthered in this citie, and ye have filled the streets thereof with the slain.
11.7: Therefore thus saith the Lord God, They that ye have slain, and have layed in the middes of it, they are the flesh, and this citie is the caldron, but I wil bring you foorth of the mids of it.
11.8: Ye have feared the sword, and I wil bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord God.
11.9: And I will bring you out of the middes thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute iudgements among you.
11.10: Ye shall fall by the sword, and I wil judge you in the border of Israel, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
11.11: This citie shall not be your caldron, neyther shall ye be the flesh in the middes thereof, but I will judge you in the border of Israel.
11.12: And ye shall know that I am the Lord: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my iudgements, but have done after the maners of the heathen, that are round about you.
11.13: And when I prophesied, Pelatiah the sonne of Benaiah dyed: then fell I down upon my face, and cryed with a loud voyce, and said, Ah Lord God, wilt thou then utterly destroy all the remnant of Israel?
11.14: Again the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
11.15: Sonne of man, thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred, and all the house of Israel, wholy are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, Depart ye far from the Lord: for the land is given us in possession.
11.16: Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God, Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countreis, yet wil I be to them as a litle Sanctuarie in ye countreis where they shall come.
11.17: Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God, I will gather you again from the people, and assemble you out of the countreis where ye have been scattered, and I will give you ye land of Israel.
11.18: And they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the idoles thereof, and all the abominations thereof from thence.
11.19: And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within their bowels: and I will take the stonie heart out of their bodies, and will give them an heart of flesh,
11.20: That they may walk in my statutes, and keep my iudgements, and execute them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
11.21: But upon them, whose heart is toward their idoles, and whose affection goeth after their abominations, I will lay their way upon their own heades, saith the Lord God.
11.22: Then did the Cherubims lift up their wings, and the wheeles besides them, and the glorie of the God of Israel was upon them on hie.
11.23: And the glorie of the Lord went up from the middes of the citie, and stood upon the moutaine which is toward the East side of the citie.
11.24: Afterward the Spirit took me up, and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Caldea to them that were led away captives: so the vision that I had seen, went up from me.
11.25: Then I declared unto them that were led away captives, all the things that the Lord had shewed me.

12.1: The word of the Lord also came unto me, saying,
12.2: Sonne of man, thou dwellest in the middes of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not: they have eares to hear, and hear not: for they are a rebellious house.
12.3: Therefore thou sonne of man, prepare thy stuff to goe into captiuitie, and goe foorth by day in their sight: and thou shalt pass from thy place to another place in their sight, if it be possible that they may consider it: for they are a rebellious house.
12.4: Then shalt thou bring foorth thy stuff by day in their sight as the stuff of him that goeth into captiuitie: and thou shalt go forth at even in their sight, as they that go foorth into captiuitie.
12.5: Dig thou through the wall in their sight, and cary out thereby.
12.6: In their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders, and carie it foorth in the dark: thou shalt cover thy face that thou see not the earth: for I have set thee as a sign unto the house of Israel.
12.7: And as I was commanded, so I brought forth my stuff by day, as ye stuff of one that goeth into captiuitie: and by night I digged through the wall with mine hand, and brought it forth in ye dark, and I bare it upon my shoulder in their sight.
12.8: And in the morning came the word of the Lord unto me, saying,
12.9: Sonne of man, hath not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, sayde unto thee, What doest thou?
12.10: But say thou unto them, Thus saith the Lord God, This burden concerneth the chief in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel that are among them.
12.11: Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall goe into bondage and captiuitie.
12.12: And the chiefest that is among them, shall bear upon his shoulder in the dark, and shall goe forth: they shall digge through the wall, to cary out thereby: he shall cover his face, that he see not the ground with his eies.
12.13: My net also will I spread upon him, and he shall be taken in my net, and I will bring him to Babel to the land of the Caldeans, yet shall he not see it, though he shall dye there.
12.14: And I will scatter toward euerie wind all that are about him to help him, and all his garisons, and I will draw out the sword after them.
12.15: And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall scatter them among the nations, and disperse them in the countreis.
12.16: But I will leave a litle nomber of them from the sword, from the famine, and from the pestilence, that they may declare all these abominations among the heathen, where they come, and they shall know, that I am the Lord.
12.17: Moreover, the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
12.18: Sonne of man, eat thy bread with trembling and drink thy water with trouble, and with carefulness,
12.19: And say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord God of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel, They shall eat their bread with carefulnes, and drink their water with desolation: for the land shall bee desolate from her abundance because of the crueltie of them that dwell therein.
12.20: And the cities that are inhabited, shall be left voyde, and the land shall be desolate, and yee shall know that I am the Lord.
12.21: And the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
12.22: Sonne of man, what is that proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying, The dayes are prolonged and all visions fail?
12.23: Tell them therefore, Thus sayeth the Lord God, I wil make this proverb to cease, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel: but say unto them, The daies are at hand and the effect of every vision.
12.24: For no vision shall be any more in vain, neither shall there bee any flattering divination within the house of Israel.
12.25: For I am the Lord: I wil speak, and that thing that I shall speak, shall come to pass: it shall be no more prolonged: for in your dayes, O rebellious house, will I say the thing, and will perform it, sayeth the Lord God.
12.26: Again the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
12.27: Sonne of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, The vision that hee seeth, is for many dayes to come, and he prophecieth of the times that are far off.
12.28: Therefore say unto them, Thus sayth the Lord God, All my wordes shall no longer be delayed, but that thing which I have spoken, shall be done, saith the Lord God.

13.1: And the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
13.2: Sonne of man, prophecie against the prophets of Israel, that prophecie, and say thou unto them, that prophecie out of their own hearts, Hear the word of the Lord.
13.3: Thus sayth the Lord God, Woe unto the foolish Prophets that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing.
13.4: O Israel, thy Prophets are like the foxes in the waste places.
13.5: Ye have not risen up in the gappes, neither made up the hedge for ye house of Israel, to stand in the battel in the day of the Lord.
13.6: They have seen vanitie, and lying divination, saying, The Lord sayth it, and the Lord hath not sent them: and they have made others to hope that they would cofirme the word of their prophecie.
13.7: Have ye not seen a vain vision? and have yee not spoken a lying divination? ye say, The Lord sayth it, albeit I have not spoken.
13.8: Therefore thus sayth the Lord God, Because ye have spoken vanytie and have seen lyes, therefore behold, I am agaynst you, sayth the Lord God,
13.9: And mine hand shalbe upon the Prophets that see vanity, and divine lies: they shall not be in the assemblie of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel: and yee shall know that I am the Lord God.
13.10: And therefore, because they have deceived my people, saying, Peace, and there was no peace: and one buylt up a wall, and behold, the others daubed it with untempered morter,
13.11: Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter, that it shall fall: for there shall come a great showre, and I wil send haylestones, which shall cause it to fall, and a stormie wind shall break it.
13.12: Lo, when the wall is fallen, shall it not bee sayd unto you, Where is the daubing wherewith ye have daubed it?
13.13: Therefore thus sayth the Lord God, I will cause a stormie wind to break foorth in my wrath, and a great showre shall bee in mine anger, and hailestones in mine indignation to consume it.
13.14: So I wil destroy the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the fundation thereof shalbe discovered, and it shall fal, and ye shalbe consumed in the middes thereof, and ye shall know, that I am the Lord.
13.15: Thus will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered morter, and will say unto you, The wall is no more, neither the daubers thereof,
13.16: To wit, the Prophets of Israel, which prophesie upon Jerusalem, and see visions of peace for it, and there is no peace, sayth the Lord God.
13.17: Likewise thou sonne of man, set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesie out of their own heart: and prophesie thou against them, and say,
13.18: Thus sayth the Lord God, Woe unto the women that sow pillowes under al arm holes, and make vailes upon the head of every one that standeth up, to hunt soules: will yee hunt ye soules of my people, and will yee give life to the soules that come unto you?
13.19: And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barly, and for pieces of bread to slay the soules of them that should not dye, and to give life to the soules that should not live in lying to my people, that hear your lies?
13.20: Wherefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I will have to do with your pillowes, wherewith yee hunt the soules to make them to flie, and I will tear them from your armes, and will let the soules goe, even the soules, that ye hunt to make them to flie.
13.21: Your vailes also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shalbe no more in your hands to be hunted, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
13.22: Because with your lyes yee have made the heart of the righteous sadde, whom I have not made sad, and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, by promising him life,
13.23: Therefore ye shall see no more vanitie, nor divine diuinatios: for I wil deliver my people out of your hand, and ye shall know that I am ye Lord.

14.1: Then came certain of the Elders of Israel unto me, and sat before me.
14.2: And the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
14.3: Sonne of man, these men have set up their idoles in their heart, and put the stumbling blocke of their iniquitie before their face: should I, being required, answer them?
14.4: Therefore speak unto them, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God, Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumbling blocke of his iniquitie before his face, and cometh to the Prophet, I the Lord will answer him that cometh, according to the multitude of his idoles:
14.5: That I may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all departed from me through their idoles.
14.6: Therfore say unto the house of Israel, Thus sayth the Lord God, Return, and withdraw your selves, and turn your faces from your idoles, and turn your faces from all your abominations.
14.7: For every one of the house of Israel, or of the stranger that soiourneth in Israel, which departeth from mee, and setteth up his idoles in his heart, and putteth the stumbling blocke of his iniquitie before his face, and cometh to a Prophet, for to inquire of him for me, I the Lord will answer him for my self,
14.8: And I will set my face against that man, and will make him an example and proverb, and I will cut him off from the middes of my people, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
14.9: And if the Prophet be deceived, when hee hath spoken a thing, I the Lord have deceived that Prophet, and I will stretch out mine hand upon him, and will destroy him from the middes of my people of Israel.
14.10: And they shall bear their punishment: the punishment of the Prophet shall bee even as the punishment of him that asketh,
14.11: That the house of Israel may go no more astray from mee, neither bee polluted any more with all their transgressions, but that they may be my people, and I may be their God, sayth the Lord God.
14.12: The word of the Lord came again unto me, saying,
14.13: Sonne of man, when ye land sinneth against me by committing a trespass, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and I will destroy man and beast forth of it.
14.14: Though these three men Noah, Daniel, and Job were among them, they should deliver but their own soules by their righteousnes, saith the Lord God.
14.15: If I bring noysome beastes into the land and they spoyle it, so that it bee desolate, that no man may pass through, because of beastes,
14.16: Though these three men were in the mids thereof, As I live, sayth the Lord God, they shall save neither sonnes nor daughters: they onely shalbe delivered, but the land shall be waste.
14.17: Or if I bring a sword upon this land, and say, Sword, go through the land, so that I destroy man and beast out of it,
14.18: Though these three men were in the mids thereof, As I live, sayth the Lord God, they shall deliver neither sonnes nor daughters, but they onely shall be delivered themselves.
14.19: Or if I send a pestilence into this land, and powre out my wrath upon it in blood, to destroy out of it man and beast,
14.20: And though Noah, Daniel and Job were in the middes of it, As I live, sayth the Lord God, they shall deliver neither sonne nor daughter: they shall but deliver their own soules by their righteousnes.
14.21: For thus saith the Lord God, How much more when I send my four sore iudgements upon Jerusalem, even the sword, and famine, and the noysome beast and pestilence, to destroy man and beast out of it?
14.22: Yet behold, therein shalbe left a remnant of them that shalbe caryed away both sonnes and daughters: behold, they shall come forth unto you, and ye shall see their way, and their enterprises: and ye shall be comforted, concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, even concerning al that I have brought upon it.
14.23: And they shall comfort you, when yee see their way and their enterprises: and ye shall know, that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, saith the Lord God.

15.1: And thee word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
15.2: Sonne of man, what cometh of the vine tree above all other trees? and of the vine braunch, which is among the trees of ye forest?
15.3: Shall wood bee taken thereof to doe any work? or wil men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?
15.4: Behold, it is cast in the fire to be consumed: the fire consumeth both the endes of it, and the middes of it is burnt. Is it meet for any work?
15.5: Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less shall it bee meet for any work, when the fire hath consumed it, and it is burnt?
15.6: Therefore thus sayth the Lord God, As the vine tree, that is among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire to be consumed, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
15.7: And I will set my face against them: they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall consume them: and ye shall know, that I am the Lord, when I set my face against them,
15.8: And when I make the land waste, because they have greatly offended, saith the Lord God.

16.1: Again, the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
16.2: Sonne of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations,
16.3: And say, Thus saith the Lord God unto Jerusalem, Thine habitation and thy kindred is of the land of Canaan: thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite.
16.4: And in thy natiuitie whe thou wast borne, thy navel was not cut: thou wast not washed in water to soften thee: thou wast not salted with salt, nor swadled in cloutes.
16.5: None eye pitied thee to do any of these unto thee, for to have compassion upon thee, but thou wast cast out in the open field to the contempt of thy person in ye day that thou wast borne.
16.6: And when I passed by thee, I saw thee polluted in thine own blood, and I said unto thee, whe thou wast in thy blood, Thou shalt live: even when thou wast in thy blood, I said unto thee, Thou shalt live.
16.7: I have caused thee to multiplie as the bud of the field, and thou hast increased and waxen great, and thou hast gotten excellent ornaments: thy breastes are facioned, thine hear is growen, where as thou wast naked and bare.
16.8: Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was as the time of love, and I spred my skirtes over thee, and covered thy filthines: yea, I sware unto thee, and entred into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord God, and thou becamest mine.
16.9: Then washed I thee with water: yea, I washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oyle.
16.10: I clothed thee also with broydred work, and shod thee with badgers skin: and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk.
16.11: I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thine handes, and a chain on thy neck.
16.12: And I put a frontlet upon thy face, and earings in thine eares, and a beautiful crown upon thine head.
16.13: Thus wast thou deckt with gold and silver, and thy rayment was of fine linen, and silk, and broydred work: thou didest eat fine flour, and honie and oyle, and thou wast very beautiful, and thou didest grow up into a kingdom.
16.14: And thy name was spred among the heathen for thy beautie: for it was perfite through my beautie which I had set upon thee, saith the Lord God.
16.15: Now thou didest trust in thine own beautie, and playedst the harlot, because of thy renown, and hast powred out thy fornications on every one that passed by, thy desire was to him.
16.16: And thou didest take thy garments, and deckedst thine hie places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon: the like thinges shall not come, neither hath any done so.
16.17: Thou hast also taken thy fair jewels made of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thy self images of men, and didest commit whoredom with them,
16.18: And tookest thy broydred garments, and coveredst them: and thou hast set mine oyle and my perfume before them.
16.19: My meat also, which I gave thee, as fine flour, oyle, and honie, wherewith I fedde thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet sauour: thus it was, saith the Lord God.
16.20: Moreover thou hast taken thy sonnes and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them, to be deuoured: is this thy whoredom a small matter?
16.21: That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through fire for them?
16.22: And in all thine abominations and whoredomes thou hast not remembred the dayes of thy youth, when thou wast naked and bare, and wast polluted in thy blood.
16.23: And beside all thy wickednes (wo, wo unto thee, saith the Lord God)
16.24: Thou hast also built unto thee an hie place, and hast made thee an hie place in every street.
16.25: Thou hast built thine hie place at every corner of the way, and hast made thy beautie to be abhorred: thou hast opened thy feet to every one that passed by, and multiplied thy whoredom.
16.26: Thou hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, which have great members, and hast encreased thy whoredom, to provoke me.
16.27: Behold, therefore I did stretch out mine hand over thee, and will diminish thine ordinarie, and deliver thee unto the will of them that hate thee, even to the daughters of the Philistims, which are ashamed of thy wicked way.
16.28: Thou hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast insaciable: yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied.
16.29: Thou hast moreover multiplied thy fornication from the land of Canaan unto Caldea, and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith.
16.30: How weak is thine heart, saith the Lord God, seeing thou doest all these thinges, even the work of a presumptuous whorish woman?
16.31: In that thou buildest thine hie place in the corner of every way, and makest thine hie place in every street, and hast not been as an harlot that despiseth a reward,
16.32: But as a wife that playeth the harlot, and taketh others for her husband:
16.33: They give giftes to all other whores, but thou givest giftes unto all thy lovers, and rewardest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy fornication.
16.34: And the contrary is in thee from other women in thy fornications, neither the like fornication shall be after thee: for in that thou givest a reward, and no reward is given unto thee, therefore thou art contrary.
16.35: Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the Lord.
16.36: Thus sayeth the Lord God, Because thy shame was powred out, and thy filthiness discovered through thy fornications with thy lovers, and with all the idoles of thine abominations, and by the blood of thy children, which thou didest offer unto them,
16.37: Behold, therefore I wil gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with al them that thou hast hated: I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy filthines unto them, that they may see all thy filthines.
16.38: And I wil judge thee after ye maner of them that are harlots, and of them that shead blood, and I wil give thee the blood of wrath and ielousie.
16.39: I will also give thee into their handes, and they shall destroy thine hie place, and shall break down thine hie places. they shall strip thee also out of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare.
16.40: They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swordes.
16.41: And they shall burn up thine houses with fire, and execute iudgements upon thee in the sight of many women: and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou shalt give no reward any more.
16.42: So will I make my wrath toward thee to rest, and my ielousie shall depart from thee, and I will cease and be no more angrie.
16.43: Because thou hast not remembred the dayes of thy youth, but hast provoked me with all these things, behold, therefore I also have brought thy way upon thine head, sayeth the Lord God: yet hast not thou had consideration of all thine abominations.
16.44: Behold, all that use prouerbes, shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.
16.45: Thou art thy mothers daughter, that hath cast off her husband and her children, and thou art the sister of thy sisters, which forsook their husbands and their children: your mother is an Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
16.46: And thine elder sister is Samaria, and her daughters, that dwell at thy left hand, and thy yong sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom, and her daughters.
16.47: Yet hast thou not walked after their wayes, nor done after their abominations: but as it had been a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more then they in all thy wayes.
16.48: As I live, saith the Lord God, Sodom thy sister hath not done, neither she nor her daughters, as thou hast done and thy daughters.
16.49: Behold, this was the iniquitie of thy sister Sodom, Pride, fulness of bread, and aboundance of idleness was in her, and in her daughters: neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needie.
16.50: But they were hautie, and committed abomination before mee: therefore I took them away, as pleased me.
16.51: Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sinnes, but thou hast exceeded them in thine abominations, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations, which thou hast done.
16.52: Therefore thou which hast justified thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sinnes, that thou hast committed more abominable then they which are more righteous then thou art: be thou therefore confounded also, and bear thy shame, seeing that thou hast justified thy sisters.
16.53: Therefore I will bring again their captiuitie with the captiuitie of Sodom, and her daughters, and with the captiuitie of Samaria, and her daughters: even the captiuitie of thy captives in the middes of them,
16.54: That thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest bee confounded in all that thou hast done, in that thou hast comforted them.
16.55: And thy sister Sodom and her daughters shall return to their former state: Samaria also and her daughters shall return to their former state, when thou and thy daughters shall return to your former state.
16.56: For thy sister Sodom was not heard of by thy report in the day of thy pride,
16.57: Before thy wickednes was discovered, as in that same time of the reproch of the daughters of Aram, and of all the daughters of the Philistims round about her which despise thee on all sides.
16.58: Thou hast borne therefore thy wickedness and thine abomination, saith the Lord.
16.59: For thus saith the Lord God, I might even deal with thee, as thou hast done: when thou didest despise the othe, in breaking the covenant.
16.60: Nevertheless, I wil remember my covenant made with thee in ye dayes of thy youth, and I wil confirm unto thee an everlasting covenant.
16.61: Then thou shalt remember thy wayes, and be ashamed, when thou shalt receive thy sisters, both thy elder and thy yonger, and I will give them unto thee for daughters, but not by thy couenat.
16.62: And I wil establish my covenant with thee, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord,
16.63: That thou mayest remember, and be ashamed, and never open thy mouth any more: because of thy shame when I am pacified toward thee, for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord God.

17.1: And the word of the Lord came unto mee, saying,
17.2: Sonne of man, put foorth a parable and speak a proverb unto the house of Israel,
17.3: And say, Thus saith the Lord God, The great eagle with great wings, and long wings, and ful of fethers, which had divers colours, came unto Lebanon, and took the highest branch of the cedar,
17.4: And brake off the toppe of his twigge, and caried it into the land of marchants, and set it in a citie of marchants.
17.5: Hee took also of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful ground: hee placed it by great waters, and set it as a willow tree.
17.6: And it budded up, and was like a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward it, and the rootes thereof were under it: so it became a vine, and it brought foorth branches, and shot foorth buds.
17.7: There was also another great eagle with great wings and many feathers, and behold, this vine did turn her rootes toward it, and spred foorth her branches toward it, that she might water it by the trenches of her plantation.
17.8: It was planted in a good soyle by great waters, that it should bring forth branches, and bear fruit, and be an excellent vine.
17.9: Say thou, Thus saith the Lord God, Shall it prosper? shall he not pull up the rootes thereof, and destroy the fruit thereof, and cause them to drie? all the leaves of her bud shall wither without great power, or many people, to pluck it up by the rootes thereof.
17.10: Behold, it was planted: but shall it prosper? shall it not be dried up, and wither? when the East wind shall touch it, it shall wither in the trenches, where it grew.
17.11: Moreover, the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
17.12: Say now to this rebellious house, Know ye not, what these things mean? tell them, Behold, the King of Babel is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the King thereof, and the princes thereof, and led them with him to Babel,
17.13: And hath taken one of the Kings seed, and made a covenant with him, and hath taken an othe of him: he hath also taken the princes of the land,
17.14: That the kingdom might be in subiection, and not lift it self up, but keep their covenant, and stand to it.
17.15: But he rebelled against him, and sent his ambassadours into Egypt, that they might give him horses, and much people: shall hee prosper? shall he escape, that doeth such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered?
17.16: As I live, saith the Lord God, he shall die in the middes of Babel, in the place of the King, that had made him King, whose othe he despised, and whose covenant made with him, he brake.
17.17: Neither shall Pharaoh with his mightie host, and great multitude of people, mainteine him in the war, when they have cast up mounts, and builded ramparts to destroy many persons.
17.18: For he hath despised the othe, and broken ye covenant (yet lo, he had given his hand) because he hath done all these things, he shall not escape.
17.19: Therefore, thus sayth the Lord God, As I live, I wil surely bring mine othe that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken upon his own head.
17.20: And I wil spread my net upon him, and he shalbe taken in my net, and I wil bring him to Babel, and will enter into iudgement with him there for his trespas that he hath committed against me.
17.21: And all that flee from him with all his host, shall fall by the sword, and they that remain, shalbe scattered toward all the windes: and ye shall know that I the Lord have spoken it.
17.22: Thus saith the Lord God, I wil also take off the top of this hie cedar, and wil set it, and cut off the top of the tender plant thereof, and I wil plant it upon an hie mountain and great.
17.23: Even in the hie mountain of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughes and bear fruit, and be an excellent cedar, and under it shall remain all birds, and every fowl shall dwell in the shadow of the branches thereof.
17.24: And all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord have brought down the hie tree, and exalted the low tree, that I have dried up the green tree, and made the drie tree to florish: I the Lord have spoken it, and have done it.

18.1: The word of the Lord came unto me again, saying,
18.2: What mean ye that ye speak this proverb, concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sowre grapes, and the childrens teeth are set on edge?
18.3: As I live, sayth the Lord God, ye shall use this proverb no more in Israel.
18.4: Behold, all soules are mine, both the soul of the father, and also the soul of the sonne are mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
18.5: But if a man be just, and doe that which is lawful, and right,
18.6: And hath not eaten upon the mountaines, neither hath lift up his eyes to the idoles of the house of Israel, neither hath defiled his neighbours wife, neither hath lyen with a menstruous woman,
18.7: Neither hath oppressed any, but hath restored the pledge to his dettour: he that hath spoyled none by violence, but hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked with a garment,
18.8: And hath not given foorth upon vsurie, neither hath taken any increase, but hath withdrawen his hand from iniquitie, and hath executed true iudgement between man and man,
18.9: And hath walked in my statutes, and hath kept my iudgements to deal truely, he is just, he shall surely live, sayth the Lord God.
18.10: If he beget a sonne, that is a thief, or a sheader of blood, if he do any one of these things,
18.11: Though he doe not all these things, but either hath eaten upon the mountaines, or defiled his neighbours wife,
18.12: Or hath oppressed the poor and needy, or hath spoyled by violence, or hath not restored the pledge, or hath lift up his eyes unto the idoles, or hath committed abomination,
18.13: Or hath given forth upon vsurie, or hath taken increase, shall he live? he shall not live: seeing he hath done all these abominations, he shall die the death, and his blood shall be upon him.
18.14: But if he beget a sonne, that seeth all his fathers sinnes, which he hath done, and feareth, neither doeth such like,
18.15: That hath not eaten upon the mountaines, neither hath lift up his eyes to the idols of ye house of Israel, nor hath defiled his neighbours wife,
18.16: Neither hath oppressed any, nor hath withholden the pledge, neither hath spoyled by violence, but hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked with a garment,
18.17: Neither hath withdrawen his hand from the afflicted, nor received vsurie nor increase, but hath executed my iudgements, and hath walked in my statutes, he shall not die in the iniquitie of his father, but he shall surely live.
18.18: His father, because he cruelly oppressed and spoyled his brother by violence, and hath not done good among his people, loe, even he dyeth in his iniquitie.
18.19: Yet say ye, Wherefore shall not the sonne bear the iniquitie of the father? because ye sonne hath executed iudgement and justice, and hath kept all my statutes, and done them, he shall surely live,
18.20: The same soul that sinneth, shall die: the sonne shall not bear the iniquitie of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquitie of the sonne, but the righteousnes of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him self.
18.21: But if the wicked will return from all his sinnes that he hath committed, and keep all my statutes, and doe that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live, and shall not die.
18.22: All his transgressions that he hath committed, they shall not be mentioned unto him, but in his righteousnes that he hath done, he shall live.
18.23: Have I any desire that the wicked should die, sayth the Lord God? or shall he not live, if he return from his wayes?
18.24: But if the righteous turn away from his righteousnes, and commit iniquitie, and doe according to all the abominations, that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? all his righteousnes that he hath done, shall not be mentioned: but in his transgression that he hath committed, and in his sinne that he hath sinned, in them shall he die.
18.25: Yet ye say, The way of the Lord is not equal: hear now, O house of Israel. Is not my way equal? or are not your wayes unequal?
18.26: For when a righteous man turneth away from his righteousnes, and committeth iniquitie, he shall even die for the same, he shall even die for his iniquitie, that he hath done.
18.27: Again when the wicked turneth away from his wickednes that he hath committed, and doeth that which is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive.
18.28: Because he considereth, and turneth away from all his transgressions that hee hath committed, he shall surely live and shall not die.
18.29: Yet saith ye house of Israel, The way of the Lord is not equal. O house of Israel, are not my wayes equal? or are not your wayes unequal?
18.30: Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his wayes, sayth the Lord God: return therefore and cause others to turn away from all your transgressions: so iniquitie shall not be your destruction.
18.31: Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby ye have transgressed, and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die, O house of Israel?
18.32: For I desire not the death of him that dyeth, sayth the Lord God: cause therefore one another to return, and live ye.

19.1: Thou also, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,
19.2: And say, Wherefore lay thy mother as a lyonesse among the lyons? she nourished her yong ones among the lyons whelps,
19.3: And she brought up one of her whelps, and it became a lyon, and it learned to catch the pray, and it deuoured men.
19.4: The nations also heard of him, and he was taken in their nets, and they brought him in chaines unto the land of Egypt.
19.5: Now when she saw, that she had waited and her hope was lost, she took another of her whelps, and made him a lyon.
19.6: Which went among the lyons, and became a lyon, and learned to catch the pray, and he deuoured men.
19.7: And he knew their widowes, and he destroyed their cities, and the land was wasted, and all that was therein by the noyse of his roaring.
19.8: Then the nations set against him on every side of the countreys, and laid their nets for him: so he was taken in their pit.
19.9: And they put him in prison and in chaines, and brought him to the King of Babel, and they put him in holdes, that his voyce should no more be heard upon the mountaines of Israel.
19.10: Thy mother is like a vine in thy blood, planted by the waters: she brought foorth fruit and branches by the abundant waters,
19.11: And she had strong rods for the scepters of them that bear rule, and her stature was exalted among the branches, and she appeared in her height with the multitude of her branches.
19.12: But she was plucked up in wrath: she was cast down to the ground, and the East wind dried up her fruit: her branches were broken, and withered: as for the rod of her strength, the fire consumed it.
19.13: And now she is planted in the wildernes in a drie and thirstie ground.
19.14: And fire is gone out of a rod of her branches, which hath deuoured her fruit, so that she hath no strong rod to be a scepter to rule: this is a lamentation and shalbe for a lamentation.

20.1: And in the seventh yeere, in the fift moneth, the tenth day of the moneth, came certain of the elders of Israel to enquire of the Lord, and sat before me.
20.2: Then came the word of the Lord unto me, saying,
20.3: Sonne of man, speak unto the Elders of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God, Are ye come to enquire of me? as I live, sayth the Lord God, when I am asked, I wil not answer you.
20.4: Wilt thou judge them, sonne of man? wilt thou judge them? cause them to understand the abominations of their fathers,
20.5: And say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God, In the day when I chose Israel, and lift up mine hand unto the seed of the house of Iaakob, and made my self knowen unto them in the land of Egypt, when I lift up mine hand unto them, and sayd, I am the Lord your God,
20.6: In the day that I lift up mine hand unto them to bring them forth of the land of Egypt, into a land that I had provided for them, flowing with milk and hony which is pleasant among all lands,
20.7: Then sayd I unto them, Let every man cast away the abominations of his eyes, and defile not your selves with the idols of Egypt: for I am the Lord your God.
20.8: But they rebelled against me, and would not hear me: for none cast away the abominations of their eyes, neither did they forsake the idoles of Egypt: then I thought to powre out mine indignation upon them, and to accomplish my wrath against them in the mids of the land of Egypt.
20.9: But I had respect to my Name, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, among whom they were, and in whose sight I made my self knowen unto them in bringing them forth of the land of Egypt.
20.10: Now I caried them out of the land of Egypt, and brought them into the wildernes.
20.11: And I gave them my statutes, and declared my iudgements unto them, which if a man doe, he shall live in them.
20.12: Moreover I gave them also my Sabbaths to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord, that sanctifie them.
20.13: But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wildernes: they walked not in my statutes, and they cast away my iudgements, which if a man doe, he shall live in them, and my Sabbaths have they greatly polluted: then I thought to powre out mine indignation upon them in the wildernes to consume them,
20.14: But I had respect to my Name, that it should not bee polluted before the heathen in whose sight I brought them out.
20.15: Yet nevertheless, I lift up mine hand unto them in the wildernes that I would not bring them into the land, which I had given them, flowing with milk and hony, which was pleasant above all landes,
20.16: Because they cast away my judgments, and walked not in my statutes, but have polluted my Sabbaths: for their heart went after their idoles.
20.17: Nevertheless, mine eye spared them, that I would not destroy them, neither would I consume them in the wildernes.
20.18: But I said unto their children in the wildernes, Walk ye not in the ordinances of your fathers, neither observe their maners, nor defile your selves with their idoles.
20.19: I am the Lord your God: walk in my statutes, and keep my iudgements and doe them,
20.20: And sanctifie my Sabbaths, and they shall bee a sign between mee and you, that ye may know that I am the Lord your God.
20.21: Notwithstanding the children rebelled against mee: they walked not in my statutes, nor kept my iudgements to doe them, which if a man doe, hee shall live in them, but they polluted my Sabbaths: then I thought to powre out mine indignation upon them, and to accomplish my wrath against them in the wildernes.
20.22: Nevertheless I withdrew mine hand and had respect to my Name that it should not be polluted before the heathen, in whose sight I brought them foorth.
20.23: Yet I lift up mine hand unto them in the wildernes, that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countreys,
20.24: Because they had not executed my iudgements, but had cast away my statutes and had polluted my Sabbaths, and their eyes were after their fathers idoles.
20.25: Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and iudgements, wherein they should not live.
20.26: And I polluted them in their own giftes in that they caused to pass by the fire all that first openeth ye womb, that I might destroy them, to the end, that they might know that I am ye Lord.
20.27: Therefore, sonne of man, speak unto the house of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God, Yet in this your fathers have blasphemed me, though they had before grieuously transgressed against me.
20.28: For when I had brought them into the land, for the which I lifted up mine hand to give it to them, then they saw every hie hill, and all the thick trees, and they offred there their sacrifices, and there they presented their offering of provocation: there also they made their sweet sauour, and powred out there their drink offerings.
20.29: Then I said unto them, What is the hie place whereunto ye goe? And the name thereof was called Bamah unto this day.
20.30: Wherefore, say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord God, Are ye not polluted after the maner of your fathers? and commit ye not whoredom after their abominations?
20.31: For when you offer your giftes, and make your sonnes to pass through the fire, you pollute your selves with all your idoles unto this day: shall I answer you when I am asked, O house of Israel? As I live, saith the Lord God, I wil not answer you when I am asked.
20.32: Neither shall that be done that cometh into your mind: for ye say, We wil be as the heathen, and as the families of the countreys, and serve wood, and stone.
20.33: As I live, saith the Lord God, I will surely rule you with a mightie hand, and with a stretched out arm, and in my wrath powred out,
20.34: And will bring you from the people, and will gather you out of the countreys, wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and in my wrath powred out,
20.35: And I will bring you into the wildernes of the people, and there wil I plead with you face to face.
20.36: Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wildernes of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you, saith the Lord God.
20.37: And I wil cause you to pass under the rod, and wil bring you into the bond of the covenant.
20.38: And I wil chuse out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against mee: I will bring them out of the land where they dwel, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
20.39: As for you, O house of Israel, thus saith the Lord God, Goe you, and serve every one his idol, seeing that ye will not obey me, and pollute mine holy Name no more with your giftes and with your idoles.
20.40: For in mine holy mountain, even in the hie mountain of Israel, saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel, and all in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offrings and the first fruites of your oblations, with all your holy things.
20.41: I will accept your sweet sauour, when I bring you from the people, and gather you out of the countreys, wherein ye have been scattered, that I may be sanctified in you before ye heathen.
20.42: And ye shall know, that I am the Lord, when I shall bring you into the land of Israel, into the land, for the which I lifted up mine hand to give it to your fathers.
20.43: And there shall ye remember your wayes, and all your workes, wherein ye have been defiled, and ye shall judge your selves worthy to be cut off, for all your evils, that ye have committed.
20.44: And ye shall know, that I am the Lord, when I have respect unto you for my Names sake, and not after your wicked wayes, nor according to your corrupt workes, O ye house of Israel, saith the Lord God.
20.45: Moreover, the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
20.46: Sonne of man, set thy face toward the way of Teman, and drop thy word toward the South, and prophecie toward the forest of the field of the South,
